scope: Proposition 4.5 (Uniform correlation test) of the manuscript “Monochromatic finite sums and products in the positive integers” (preprints/Monochromatic-finite-sums-and-products-in-the-positive-integers-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 164 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ab835f6a98c10d6d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 27. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every m ≥ 2 and every nonsingleton target support J∗, the construction above determines a finite family of integer polynomial templates D, with good prime-tuple laws, such that the following holds for every fixed master chain and valid gap l. There are an integer 1 ≤ d ≤ Km − 1, a constant Cm, and θ > 0, all bounded in terms of m alone, for which |C| ≤ o(1) + Cm ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ Ep,y,u ∏︂ ω⊆[d] g∗ (︄ y + M(p) ∑︂ R∈ω (u1 R − u0 R) )︄⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ ⃓ θ . (4.17) Here y has law µia∗ , independently of the primes and shifts; the primes have the normalized good-tuple law of Lemma 4.3; M(p) is given by (4.9); and the shifts have the conditional laws in (4.12). One may take θ = 2−(qmask+d). The gap length Rl is divisible by every M(p) that occurs. The estimate is uniform over all the masks and functions in (4.1), including g∗, and over each fixed finite set of positive integers J0. Neither d, Cm, nor θ−1 depends on N, on the scales, or on the functions. The polynomial templates and direction choices are fixed before M and the prime pools are chosen. In particular, the same tests can be used both for a bounded error and for an error bounded by 1 + νa∗ .
